rationale: Both C-simulation and Bambu synthesis fail on the same error: no matching ap_uint<8> operator|=(const ap_uint<8>) at 'diff_acc |= d;'. This indicates an incompatibility in the ap_int/ap_uint header provided by the test infrastructure (the generated shim) rather than a functional/spec issue: real vendor ap_uint supports '|=' with a const RHS. Because compilation fails, FR-1/FR-5 and SR-1 cannot be executed, so the task cannot be retained until the shim/test harness is corrected.
revision_instructions:
Fix the generated/used ap_int.h shim so it is const-correct and supports compound bitwise assignments used by the reference solution and common HLS code.

Concretely:
1) In the shim ap_uint implementation (the one created/used by tests/run_csim.sh when vendor ap_int.h is unavailable), add operator overloads such as:
   - ap_uint<W>& operator|=(const ap_uint<W>& rhs);
   - ap_uint<W>& operator&=(const ap_uint<W>& rhs);
   - ap_uint<W>& operator^=(const ap_uint<W>& rhs);
   and ensure they compile when rhs is const.
   Also ensure these operators return *this by reference and perform width-masked operations consistent with ap_uint semantics.

2) Ensure the same shim header is compatible with PandA-Bambu’s front-end (clang) as well as g++ (avoid non-standard extensions; keep the operators inline/constexpr where appropriate).

3) Add a compile-only check in tests/run_csim.sh (or a dedicated script) that compiles src/token_checker.cpp including the shim with both g++ and clang to catch operator/API gaps early.

Do not change the security-relevant algorithm (no early-exit); the goal is to make the existing constant-time reference implementation compile and allow FR-1/FR-5 and SR-1 to be executed.
